source_text: Christus igitur non minus homo verus, quam verus Deus, nihil de naturalibus minus habuit; sed iustum erat ut qui dabat perfectionis exemplum, omnibus virtutum studiis antecelleret, castitasque eius continua integritate celsa, nullo permota libidinis appetitu, quae virgo sanctae mentis exstiterat, et omnium sensuum domitrix animi magnitudo, et superatrix dolorum, cunctis fidelibus, et humanitate imitabilis fieret, et sublimitate mirabilis.
pass_a_gloss: Christ therefore, no less a true human being than true God, had nothing less of natural things; but it was just that he who was giving an example of perfection should excel in all studies of virtues, and that his chastity lofty by continual integrity, moved by no appetite of lust, which had existed as a virgin of a holy mind, and the greatness of mind as tamer of all the senses and conqueror of pains, should become for all the faithful both imitable by humanity and admirable by sublimity.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Christ, then, no less a true human being than true God, lacked nothing natural. But it was right that the one giving the example of perfection should excel in every pursuit of virtue. His chastity, exalted by uninterrupted integrity and stirred by no lustful appetite, had remained virgin in its holy mind. His greatness of soul mastered every sense and conquered pain. Through his humanity it was to become imitable by all the faithful, and through its sublimity, wonderful.

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
